oracle.P2: eshop-sut/README.md line 195 — product name: required, at most 255 characters

note: No status code is asserted anywhere. api_specification.md §3.3 documents only the request body for the product write endpoints — no success status, no error contract, no status code in the whole document. HW02 froze these expectations at outcome level for exactly that reason: 'the create is rejected, OR if created, it must not be persisted with X'. Both shapes are compliant and both must pass.
globalStateNote: Products are GLOBAL state — they belong to no user and are shared by every worker, project and previous run. Every case therefore (a) tags its payload with a unique marker in `description`, (b) targets ONLY the row it created, via the id returned by POST, and (c) NEVER asserts on a total product count. A count assertion would be broken by any parallel worker.
schemaNote: input.name.mode: 'literal' sends the given value; 'omit' leaves the key off the body entirely; 'uniqueOfLength' generates a name of EXACTLY that many characters that still begins with the test's unique marker, so a length boundary and global uniqueness hold at the same time. expected.persistence.compareTo: 'sentValue' compares the read-back field against what this test actually sent; 'literal' compares against the given literal.

cases.technique: BVA — `price` at the minimum valid value (1), plus an endpoint-consistency check on the same rows
cases.title: A price of 1 is valid and persists, and both read endpoints agree about it

expected.assertionNote: Owns BUG-15-102 (issue #9). The oracle is that GET /api/products/:id and GET /api/products report the SAME price for the SAME product — it never mentions ids, parity or toString(). Parity is used only to SELECT inputs: the case holds one product of each id parity so the class where the SUT can differ is actually exercised, rather than passing vacuously on an odd id. That vacuous pass is exactly the false pass finding 70 was about.

cases.title: Editing one product in the admin panel must leave other products' displayed names unchanged

expected.assertionNote: Judged INDEPENDENTLY of TC-15-EP-010. That case passed, proving the BACKEND isolates edits correctly — which says nothing about what the admin panel renders. The sibling's displayed name is recorded from the table BEFORE the edit and compared afterwards, so the oracle is 'unchanged from its own recorded original'. Must be observed WITHOUT reloading: a refetch would repopulate the table from the backend and hide a client-state defect.
